slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
content_zh:
陈默记得的最后画面，是一尊青铜神像之眼。
那是四川广汉三星堆遗址第七号祭祀坑发掘现场。下午四点十七分，他站在三米深的探方底部，手中毛刷刚拂去一尊高约两米的青铜纵目面具上最后一丝浮土。面具双目向外凸出呈圆柱状，在斜阳下反射诡异青铜光泽，仿佛不是死物，而是某个被封印了两千年活体正试图睁开眼睛。
就在那个瞬间，脚下传来一下极轻微震动。像远处有辆重型卡车驶过，又像地壳深处某个沉睡已久的东西翻了身。考古队有人抬头喊了句“地震了“，陈默本能地护住青铜面具想往安全位置挪动，但他还没来得及迈出第二步，脚下探方就真的裂开了。
不是比喻。一条漆黑裂缝从他两脚之间劈开，像刀刃切入豆腐般迅速扩大。脚底泥土塌陷时他试图后退，身体却已浮空。青铜面具在他眼前滑入裂缝——那双凸出柱状眼瞳在坠落前最后看了他一眼，然后被黑暗吞没。他跟着掉了下去，没有叫出声，因为胸腔被迅速灌入某种高压气流封住了喉咙。
坠落过程漫长而失真。四周黑暗有质感，像液态活物环绕着他缓慢蠕动。他伸手去抓，手指穿过黑暗什么也没碰到。失重忽然消失，取而代之是被静滞于琥珀的悬浮感——时间、声音、重力全部暂停。
然后是光。极亮纯白光从四面同时涌来，穿透眼皮、皮肤、颅骨——仿佛每个细胞都被翻开逐层审视。在光深处，他看到了某种不该出现在任何人认知中的景象。
一片悬浮在无尽紫色虚空的光点群，数以万计，没有天幕背景。每一颗光点都是一只眼睛——竖瞳、圆瞳、裂瞳、数不清的瞳——全都在缓缓转动，朝向他所在方位聚拢。陈默想尖叫，但他的身体、喉咙、肺叶全部脱离他。那片“星空“不对劲，不是因为它在看人，而是因为它一直知道会有一个人从外面来。
***
他听到第一声喊叫是用一种他没学过的语言发出，但他竟然听得懂，好像那种语言***早就被预装在他脑中了。他的喉咙干得像砂纸，眼皮重如铅块，四肢贴着粗糙亚麻床单的印象既陌生又清晰。急促脚步声、金属甲叶碰撞脆响、某种低沉有韵律祈祷词——这些声音从不同的方向涌来，在他的意识中拼成一幅模糊图景。然后一束暖金色光落在脸上，不是阳光——它透过某种彩色玻璃照进来，落在皮肤上时带起一阵微弱刺痛，像极其细微静电放电。
他费力睁开眼睛。一张年轻女性的脸出现在视野中——约莫二十三四岁，栗色长发束成高马尾，几缕碎发黏在汗湿的额角上。她的琥珀色眼睛里满是焦虑和压抑的慌乱，那是战场上目睹死亡后残留的表情。她穿着一件白色镶金的胸甲，甲胄上刻着一枚纹章：展翅雄鹰环绕满月。那图案陈默从未见过，却在注视瞬间产生莫名熟悉感，像在照片中看到自己从没去过的故乡。
“雷诺！你听得见我说话吗？“她的声音急切但不失控制，带着一线希望被救助者活下来的恳求。
雷诺。他在脑海中搜索这两个字，没有任何匹配。他想开口纠正她，但喉咙只发出一声沙哑的咳嗽，像生锈的铁门被强行推开。
“别动，你伤得很重，牧师马上到。“她伸手按住他的肩膀，力道轻而稳，“你被抬回来的时候全身都是血，我们都以为你——“话被沉重脚步声截断。陈默转动眼球，看到一个穿深红袍子的中年男人走了进来，双手捧着一本厚重皮面书和一只水晶圣杯。那男人在床前停下，翻开书，用一种低沉而庄严的声调开始诵读。陈默听不懂那些词语，但他感觉到了空气的变化——什么东西被唤醒了。
圣杯中液体开始发光。暖金色从杯底升起，像一团被封在玻璃中的火焰。中年男人将手指浸入圣杯，然后在他额头上画了一个符号。冰凉从符号渗入颅骨，紧接着脑海中涌入了无数画面——雪地中的战场、在寒风中猎猎作响的破碎旗帜、一把锈蚀长剑刺入胸口的剧痛、寒冷泥土灌入嘴里的窒息感、一个骑着黑马的人影在他倒下前俯视着他。然后是无限、无边无际黑暗，比他在裂缝中坠落时经历的更深。
那些记忆不属于他，但他知道它们的主人是谁。雷诺·艾德伍德，二十五岁，骑士学院肄业生，艾德伍德家族最后一滴血脉，一个在边境战役中受了致命伤的没落贵族。记忆被解码的那个瞬间，陈默的意识从混乱中浮现，变得极其冷静——穿越了。。不是回到古代中国，不是进入某个历史时期，而是来到了一个完全陌生、同时存在着骑士、魔法和圣光的世界。他的灵魂进入了这个叫雷诺的年轻人体内，而这个人身体中残留的全部记忆正在他的脑海中展开。
作为一个研究比较神话学的博士生，他读过太多关于“穿越““转世““灵魂转移“的文本——从柏拉图的洞穴寓言之于灵魂升维，到《桃花源记》的时空错位，从藏地转世灵童的认定仪轨到凯尔特神话中的异界水渡。在学术层面，这些都是文化符号和隐喻系统。当它真的发生时，他的第一反应不是恐惧，而是一种既冰冷又炽热的兴奋——他活着见证了神话学假设变成现实，而他恰好是唯一有知识储备去理解这一事件的人。
“你还好吗？“女骑士的声音把他拉回现实，“你的眼神很奇怪——像是变了一个人。“
陈默——顶着雷诺的脸和身体——慢慢点了点头。他在脑海中搜索雷诺记忆，找到了她的名字。艾莉西亚·晨曦，晨曦家族次女，圣殿骑士团见习骑士，雷诺在骑士学院的同级生。“艾莉西亚，我没事。“这是他来到这个世界说的第一句话。他不会知道，当他开口的那一瞬间，那个正在施法的红袍牧师突然停了下来。牧师手指在圣杯上方微微颤抖，某种极淡、几乎不可见的紫色光芒在水面上闪烁了一瞬，然后消失。牧师抬起头，用一阵复杂的目光看着床上这个年轻人，没有对任何人说出他所看到的。
***
三天后，陈默从床上站起来，第一次走出了医疗所。埃尔德兰的阳光落在脸上——温暖、真实、带着淡淡的草木焚烧的气息，和他在地球上闻过的任何一种空气都不一样。靴子踩在石板路上发出坚实声响，街道两侧是尖顶石砌建筑，拱窗上镶着彩绘玻璃，铁艺招牌在微风中轻轻晃动。穿亚麻布衣的商贩在叫卖，戴头巾的主妇蹲在井边打水，几个穿皮甲的士兵靠在墙根晒太阳。这一切看起来就像一座中世纪欧洲主题影城——但陈默知道不是，因为他抬起头看到了天空。

白天本不该看到星星，但这片天空东北角有一组星群在日光中依然清晰可见，呈现出一种不应存在于自然界的排列方式。它们像是有人用圆规和直尺在天幕上画了一个精确几何图形——八个点构成一个类圆形阵列，中心位置留空。陈默盯着那组星群看了很久。他熟悉希腊星座划分体系、中国二十八星宿的官制、玛雅古籍中的金星周期表和埃及天文学中的旬星系统，但天上这个图案不属于他已知的任何文明。
“你在看什么？“艾莉西亚从身后走来，顺着他的目光看了天空一眼，“那是常耀星群，据说是诸神的王座，它们一直都在那里。“
“一直？从什么时候开始？“
她愣了一下，显然从没想过这个问题。“从——有记载以来？创世神话里说，乱世之光化为星辰照耀万物，那些亮星是神之目光的见证。“
content_en:
The last image Chen Mo remembered was the eye of a bronze statue.
That was the excavation site of the No. 7 sacrificial pit at the Sanxingdui site in Guanghan, Sichuan. At 4:17 in the afternoon, he stood at the bottom of the three-meter-deep Tanfang. The brush in his hand had just brushed off the last trace of loose soil on a bronze longitudinal mask about two meters high. The mask's eyes protrude outward in a cylindrical shape, reflecting a strange bronze luster under the setting sun, as if it is not a dead object, but a living body that has been sealed for two thousand years and is trying to open its eyes.
At that moment, there was a very slight vibration under my feet. It was like a heavy truck passing by in the distance, or like something deep in the earth's crust that had been sleeping for a long time and turned over. Someone from the archaeological team raised his head and shouted, "There's an earthquake." Chen Mo instinctively protected the bronze mask and tried to move to a safe position, but before he could take the second step, Tan Fang really cracked under his feet.
Not a metaphor. A dark crack split between his feet, expanding rapidly like a knife cutting into tofu. When the soil beneath his feet collapsed, he tried to retreat, but his body was already floating in the air. The bronze mask slipped into the cracks in front of his eyes - the bulging columnar eyes glanced at him one last time before falling, and then were swallowed by darkness. He fell down without making a sound because some kind of high-pressure airflow was quickly poured into his chest and his throat was sealed.
The fall was long and distorted. The darkness around him had texture, like a liquid living thing slowly squirming around him. He reached for it, but his fingers touched nothing through the darkness. The weightlessness suddenly disappeared, replaced by a suspended feeling stagnant in amber - time, sound, and gravity were all suspended.
Then comes the light. Extremely bright pure white light came from all directions at the same time, penetrating the eyelids, skin, and skull - as if every cell was opened and examined layer by layer. In the depths of the light, he saw something that should not appear in anyone's mind.
A group of tens of thousands of light points suspended in the endless purple void, with no sky background. Each point of light was an eye—vertical pupils, round pupils, slit pupils, countless pupils—all slowly rotating, gathering towards his direction. Chen Mo wanted to scream, but his body, throat, and lungs were all separated from him. There's something wrong with that "starry sky", not because it's looking at people, but because it always knows there's someone coming from outside.
***
The first shout he heard was in a language he had never learned, but he actually understood it, as if the language had been pre-installed in his mind. His throat was as dry as sandpaper, his eyelids were as heavy as lead, and the image of his limbs pressed against rough linen sheets was both foreign and clear. The sound of hurried footsteps, the crunching sound of metal armor leaves, some kind of low and rhythmic prayer - these sounds came from different directions, forming a fuzzy picture in his consciousness. Then a beam of warm golden light fell on the face, and it wasn't sunlight - it was shining through some kind of stained glass, and when it fell on the skin, it caused a faint sting, like an extremely small discharge of static electricity.
He struggled to open his eyes. A young woman's face appeared in the field of vision - about twenty-three or four years old, with long chestnut hair tied into a high ponytail, with a few strands of hair stuck to her sweaty forehead. Her amber eyes were full of anxiety and suppressed panic, the expression left after witnessing death on the battlefield. She wore a white breastplate inlaid with gold, with a heraldry engraved on it: an eagle with outstretched wings surrounding the full moon. Chen Mo had never seen that pattern before, but the moment he looked at it, he felt inexplicably familiar, like seeing a hometown he had never been to in a photo.
"Reno! Can you hear me?" Her voice was urgent but controlled, with a glimmer of hope that the rescued person would survive.
Renault. He searched for these two words in his mind, but there was no match. He wanted to open his mouth to correct her, but only a hoarse cough came out of his throat, like a rusty iron door being forced open.
"Don't move. You're seriously injured. The priest will be here soon." She reached out and held his shoulders with light but steady force. "When you were carried back, your whole body was injured."It's blood, we all thought you-" The words were cut off by the sound of heavy footsteps. Chen Mo rolled his eyes and saw a middle-aged man in a dark red robe walking in, holding a thick leather book and a crystal chalice in his hands. The man stopped in front of the bed, opened the book, and began to read in a low and solemn tone. Chen Mo couldn't understand the words, but he felt the change in the air - something was awakened.
The liquid in the chalice begins to glow. Warm golden color rises from the bottom of the cup, like a flame sealed in glass. The middle-aged man dipped his finger into the chalice and drew a symbol on his forehead. The coldness penetrated from the symbol into the skull, and then countless images flooded into his mind - the battlefield in the snow, the broken flags rustling in the cold wind, the sharp pain of a rusty sword piercing his chest, the suffocating feeling of cold mud pouring into his mouth, and a figure riding a black horse looking down at him before he fell. Then came infinite, endless darkness, deeper than he had ever experienced when he fell through the rift.
Those memories didn't belong to him, but he knew who owned them. Reno Edwood, twenty-five years old, a graduate of the Knight Academy, the last drop of blood of the Edwood family, a declining nobleman who was fatally wounded in the border battle. The moment the memory was decoded, Chen Mo's consciousness emerged from the chaos and became extremely calm - traveling through time. . It's not about going back to ancient China, it's not about entering a certain historical period, but it's about coming to a completely unfamiliar world where knights, magic and holy light coexist. His soul entered the body of this young man named Renault, and all the memories remaining in this man's body were unfolding in his mind.
As a doctoral student studying comparative mythology, he has read too many texts about "travel", "reincarnation" and "soul transfer" - from Plato's allegory of the cave to the dimensionality of the soul, to the time and space dislocation in "The Peach Blossom Spring", from the identification rituals of reincarnated soul boys in Tibet to the otherworldly water crossing in Celtic mythology. At an academic level, these are systems of cultural symbols and metaphors. When it does happen, his first reaction is not fear, but a kind of cold and hot excitement - he has lived to witness the mythological hypothesis become a reality, and he happens to be the only person with the knowledge reserve to understand this event.
"Are you okay? The female knight's voice brought him back to reality, "You have a strange look in your eyes - it's like you've changed into a different person." "
Chen Mo - holding Renault's face and body - nodded slowly. He searched Renault's memory in his mind and found her name. Alicia Chenxi, the second daughter of the Chenxi family, a trainee knight of the Knights Templar, and Renault's classmate at the Knight Academy. “Alicia, I’m okay. "This was the first sentence he said when he came into this world. He would not know that the moment he spoke, the red-robed priest who was casting a spell suddenly stopped. The priest's fingers trembled slightly above the Holy Grail, and a very faint, almost invisible purple light flickered on the water for a moment, and then disappeared. The priest raised his head and looked at the young man on the bed with a complex look, without telling anyone what he saw.
***
Three days later, Chen Mo stood up from the bed and walked out of the medical center for the first time. The sunlight fell on Eldran's face - warm, real, with a faint smell of burning vegetation, different from any air he had smelled on earth. The boots made a solid sound on the stone pavement. On both sides of the street were pointed stone buildings, with stained glass on the arched windows, and wrought iron signboards swaying gently in the breeze. Vendors in linen clothes were hawking, housewives in headscarves squatted by the well to draw water, and several soldiers in leather armor leaned against the wall to bask in the sun. It all looked like a medieval European-themed movie theater - but Chen Mo knew it wasn't because he raised his head and saw the sky.
You shouldn't see stars during the day, but there is a group of stars in the northeast corner of the sky.Still visible in the light, they show an arrangement that should not exist in nature. They look like someone used a compass and ruler to draw a precise geometric figure on the canopy—eight points forming a quasi-circular array, leaving the center empty. Chen Mo stared at the group of stars for a long time. He was familiar with the Greek constellation system, the Chinese official system of twenty-eight constellations, the periodic table of Venus in Mayan ancient books, and the ten-star system in Egyptian astronomy, but this pattern in the sky did not belong to any civilization he knew.
"What are you looking at?" Alicia came up from behind and glanced at the sky along his gaze. "That's the Everlasting Stars. It's said to be the throne of the gods. They've always been there."
"Always? Since when?"
She was stunned for a moment, obviously she had never thought about this problem. "Since - since records began? The creation myth says that the light of troubled times turns into stars to shine on all things. Those bright stars are witnesses of God's gaze."
